description:
ParkScreen puts a screen from your Windows PC into your car's web browser, so you can watch or work while you are parked and waiting.

Install ParkScreen on your PC, ask it for a pairing code, and enter the 6-digit code at parkscreen.web.app in your car's browser. Your PC encodes the chosen monitor as H.264 video and sends it straight to the car over an encrypted WebRTC connection. The ParkScreen server only helps the two devices find each other: your video is never relayed, recorded or stored by us.

How it works
- Install ParkScreen. It runs quietly in the background and keeps itself up to date.
- Run parkscreen-host --pair (from the install folder) to get a pairing code that is valid for 5 minutes.
- Open https://parkscreen.web.app in your car's browser and enter the code. Your car is remembered for next time.

Good to know
- Use ParkScreen only while parked. Tesla blocks video while the car is in gear, and ParkScreen does not work around that.
- To show something other than your main monitor, extend your desktop onto a second or virtual display (for example a virtual display driver) and ParkScreen will prefer it.
- Touch control from the car is not available yet.
- Needs an internet connection on the PC and in the car, and a hardware or software H.264 encoder (most PCs have one).

Privacy: no analytics, no accounts, no ads. See the privacy policy for details.
short: Show a screen from your Windows PC in your car's browser while parked. Pair with a 6-digit code; video goes peer to peer over encrypted WebRTC.
whatsnew: First release. Pair your car with a 6-digit code and stream a PC monitor to the car's browser. Includes automatic updates.
features: Pair with a 6-digit code, remembered for next time
H.264 video with hardware encoding where available
Peer to peer encrypted WebRTC: video never passes through our servers
Streams a chosen monitor, including a virtual or extended display
